out_of_schema_notes: ProvenAcceptableRange keeps the field name par_at_setpoint for the univariate PAR (the report's 'Univ.' column, other parameters at their set-points); at this step the set-point of every design factor is the centre of its range studied.

ProcessParameter.NOR is the NOR in force. For protein load it is the NOR this revision narrowed at its upper edge; the studies were planned and run against the NOR as characterized. ProcessParameter.PAR is the narrowest NOR-propagated PAR over the outputs with a criterion for a multivariate parameter, and the range studied for a univariate one.

The schema has no record type for a discrepancy from the plan, and its Deviation model is not used for one: the report records no deviation (a process characterization study is not GMP manufacture; explicit non-claim NC10) and calls every departure from the plan a discrepancy. Each of PD-005-01 to PD-005-09 is a report statement anchored on its row of the discrepancy register, which the report prints in two parts (@tbl-pd and @tbl-pd-b, table ids PCR-005_tab_pd and PCR-005_tab_pd_b), and the studies a discrepancy adds (S-PA-SDM2, S-PA-HLD) carry that row as a source reference. PD-005-07, PD-005-08 and PD-005-09 were the Deviation records DEV-005-03, DEV-005-04 and DEV-005-05 of the annex as re-anchored to the follow-up text (config campaign.plan_discrepancies). These three, the departures found in the Version 2.0 review of the record, also have report statements anchored on the sentences of their own subsections (§13.3.3 to §13.3.5): what the plan required and what was done, how the departure was found and what was done with the runs, and why it changes no conclusion.

The hold study S-PA-HLD has no hold study type in StudyDesign.study_type and is recorded as univariate (hold time at two temperatures); its factors are not process parameters. The nrCE-SDS retest S-PA-RET has no study type and no study record. The scale-down qualification studies carry no n_runs, which the corpus test reserves for the seeded DoE designs; their run counts are in the report statements of the qualification.

The Cpk of leached Protein A is not meaningful (simulated values below the LOQ) and its index_value is empty. The mean of a capability record is the printed mean; the report gives a range, not a standard deviation.

The coefficient assertions name the most significant term of each factor in the selected model (main effect, square or interaction). Leached Protein A has a selected model with no term, so its parameter assertions come from the screening effects table.
Step yield is a performance attribute with no criterion (concept attr:step_yield).

The classification argument of §9 is carried by the parameter records (rationale_for_criticality: the significant terms, the change of pool host cell protein across the NOR-propagated PAR as a share of its criterion, the margin of the PAR to the NOR and the reason for the class, each anchored on its sentence of §9) and by one assertion per parameter and attribute that §9 names, anchored on the sentence that names them.

The 2 study events (DEV-005-01, DEV-005-02), the events of execution that Version 1.0 recorded, are Deviation records, the schema's only record for an event and what was done about it. The report calls them study events, not deviations, and keeps their Version 1.0 numbers. Each record anchors on its row of the study-event register (@tbl-dev: Event, Summary, Detected during, Outcome; disposition is the Outcome cell as printed) and on sentences of its own subsection (§13.1, §13.2); the record of DEV-005-02 also cites the sentence of the executive summary that names it. The executive summary names both events in one sentence, which anchors a report statement.

Report statements and sections keep their ids across re-anchorings. PCR-005-S01 to PCR-005-S84 are those of the annex as first fitted to the Version 2.0 text (six sections), PCR-005-S85 to PCR-005-S118 those added when it was re-anchored to the follow-up text (the sections Objectives and Design space were added then), and PCR-005-S119 to PCR-005-S143 those added when it was re-anchored to the record pass of 2026-10-10 (the study events, the discrepancies PD-005-07 to PD-005-09 and the single-run limits of the criteria table). A statement whose sentence was reworded keeps its id, and no id is retired. The section 'Deviations and discrepancies from the plan' (sec05) is retitled 'Study events and discrepancies from the plan', as §13 of the report is. The non-claim NC08 of the first fit (a design space drawn on median predictions is not a claim for a single batch) is withdrawn, because the design space is now drawn on the upper prediction limit of a single run; NC09 records that the region drawn on the median prediction is a comparison only.

parameters.rationale_for_criticality: Classified WC-CPP under SOP-4001 by the decision logic of PCMP-001 §7.7, as PCP-005 §7 criterion 7 applies it. Terms of the selected models that contain it and are significant at α 0.05 (PCMP-001 §6.2): pool host cell protein, A (p < 0.001); step yield, A (p < 0.001) and AC (p = 0.027). Across its NOR-propagated PAR for pool host cell protein, 10–50 g/L resin, pool host cell protein changes by 6,547 ng/mg at manufacturing scale with the other parameters at their set-points, 38 % of its criterion of ≤ 17,069 ng/mg. The PAR extends 10 g/L resin below and 11 g/L resin above the NOR of 20–39 g/L resin. The effect is practically relevant: with elution buffer pH it takes pool host cell protein above its criterion within the range studied, so the parameter is critical. It is readily controlled, being set from the titre of the clarified harvest, and its PAR is wide against its NOR, so it is well controlled.
